content: Reader and curate at St Helen's, Bishopsgate
He can turn the glass twice and stop, without opening a new head to fill the time.
He turns the sand-glass twice, says he will be brief, and is not brief. He counted ten days to the fast.
He reads the commination as it is written, and he enjoys the sharp sentences, and he will not read them twice.
Given an order, he can set the glass down after one turning, and then read what he was told to read.
Given the ordinance to preach, he set the glass down after one turning and did not go on.
He said he would be brief, turned the glass twice, and was not brief. On Tuesday evening he did not turn it.
He can frighten a parish more with one turn of the glass than with a long sermon.
He reaches fourteenthly, and he will not write the sermon out.
He kept All Saints to one glass because the wardens had spoken, and he would not say it again.
He reached fourteenthly and would not give the rest of it in a porch, and he did not ask to read the letter.
